---
name: vibeshape-export
description: Save editable VibeShape backups, export committed STEP/STL/3MF files, or hand off a model to a desktop slicer. Use for CAD artifact delivery; printer operation, G-code production, and model publication require separate requested workflows.
---

# VibeShape export

Use [vibeshape-use](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-use/SKILL.md) for session setup. Establish the intended saved model/revision before exporting; an exact preview does not persist a draft. Read [print preparation and handoff](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-export/references/printing.md) only when preparing a print or opening a slicer.

## Choose the artifact

| Need | Artifact |
| --- | --- |
| Editable VibeShape project with authored history | Native `.vshape` through `prepare_project_backup` or the editor's project-file controls |
| Exact geometry for another CAD application | STEP |
| Unit-aware mesh interchange for slicing | 3MF |
| Mesh compatibility with an STL-only consumer | STL; explicitly state coordinates are mm |

Native backups of projects with disconnected History inputs use `.vshape` V6 and retain the original repair recipes, downstream items, and suspended Part identities. Open them in a V6-capable editor; older readers reject this authority rather than silently dropping repair state. Geometry exports require a successfully rebuilt model.

STEP/STL/3MF are geometry exports, not native editable backups. Browser autosave remains tied to that browser origin/profile. Native **Open project (.vshape)** imports a separate copy; use it for restoring/transferring authored intent, and inspect the resulting copy before editing. Do not substitute a mesh export for a requested editable project.

## Shared MCP file transfer

When advertised, use `prepare_model_export` with exact committed `revision` and STEP/STL/3MF
`format`, or `prepare_project_backup` for an editable `.vshape`. These tools work through local
and paired remote MCP, accept no destination path and export the committed document.

For STL/3MF, optionally pass `meshQuality: { chordTolerance, angularTolerance }` with absolute
chord tolerance in millimeters (`0.005`–`1`) and angular deflection in radians (`0.01`–`0.5`).
Omit it to preserve existing export defaults: STL `0.05 mm / 0.1 rad`, 3MF `0.02 mm / 0.1 rad`.
Smaller tolerances increase curved-surface detail and file size; transfer and print budgets still
apply. Imported triangle meshes retain their source resolution. STEP rejects mesh quality.

Save the returned descriptor, then call `read_export_chunk` with its `exportId`, byte `offset`
and optional `limit` up to `chunkMaxBytes`. Decode each base64 chunk using ordinary client file
tools, append bytes in offset order and follow `nextOffset` until null. Verify final `byteLength`
and SHA-256 against the descriptor before reporting delivery. Keep binary output out of the
conversation; do not save base64 text under a CAD extension. Finish with `discard_export`.

Files are limited to 6 MiB and expire after five minutes without renewal. Only one prepared file
exists per paired actor; preparing another evicts it. Disconnect or project replacement removes
access. A later model edit does not alter detached bytes; the descriptor identifies the exported
revision. Pace remote reads under its ordinary operation rate limit and remaining session budget.
Use the browser workflow for larger files or explicit part selection. A descriptor alone is not
a delivered file.

## Legacy local MCP export

When `export_model` is advertised, call it with the exact committed `revision` and `format: "step"`, `"stl"`, or `"3mf"`. It accepts no file path and exports the committed model, not a draft or a named part selector.
Its optional `meshQuality` follows the same STL/3MF contract as the shared chunk tools.

Read the returned `resource_link.uri` through MCP resources/read. Decode the base64 blob and save the bytes with the client's ordinary file tools at the requested destination. Do not save base64 text under the geometry extension or print the blob into conversation. Current resource limit is 6 MiB and lifetime is five minutes; revoking pairing removes access. Read and save promptly.

Use the resource's filename/MIME type and revision to identify the result. Resolve an existing destination without silently overwriting unrelated work. A resource link alone is not a delivered file. Inspect saved file size/format when needed; re-import or open it in the intended consumer when interoperability is part of acceptance.

## Remote and browser export

Remote omits the legacy `export_model` binary resources; use the shared chunk tools above when
advertised. The editor's **Export model** dialog supports STEP/STL/3MF, and project-file controls
support `.vshape`. Select explicit part scope in the visible dialog when requested; hidden parts
can still be included in all-body export. Wait for ordinary saves or active CAD work to finish first.
The dialog, assembly export and **Prepare print** expose **Mesh quality** choices. **Default**
preserves each path's existing tessellation; **Coarse** uses `0.2 mm / 0.3 rad`, and **Fine**
uses `0.01 mm / 0.05 rad`. Quality changes only the disposable mesh, not authored geometry.

Use the host's download/file handling to establish the final file path. If the browser tools cannot retrieve a download, have the person complete that download and report the exact gap; do not claim delivery based on a button click. No direct storage access or internal script invocation is a substitute for the supported export path.

Finish with the artifact path or accessible delivery link, format/units, and the material validation result. Opening a slicer, obtaining G-code, uploading a public model, and physical printing are distinct outcomes.

# Print preparation and desktop handoff

Exact CAD validity does not prove wall thickness, support requirements, strength, physical fit, or slicer settings. The current MCP surface does not provide a production printability report, printer profile, toolpath, or G-code.

For a requested printable part, retain the supplied printer/material/nozzle, mating dimensions, and tolerances. If these change the design and are missing, ask before making consequential geometry or slicing choices. Separate nominal model dimensions from physical clearance assumptions and later mount/print evidence.

## Prepared-print copy

The editor's **Export → Prepare print…** creates a disposable derived copy for print preparation. It does not rewrite the saved parametric model. The current slice rotates around X/Y, centers/seats the copy, and can add up to two breakaway fins on suitable sloped planar facets of a validated convex closed body. Unsupported cases retain the transformed copy without fins and report a warning; even supported cases provide partial coverage. Use only the current dialog's requested controls. Preview the prepared copy, identify any added geometry, and keep its file distinguishable from the original export.

Prepared-copy controls are not exposed as MCP tools. Exported 3MF records millimetres; it is not a native Bambu Studio project with an established printer, process, filament, and plate profile. Avoid interpreting geometric preparation as slicing evidence.

## Native desktop handoff

The Mac and Windows desktop export dialogs send a generated STL or 3MF directly to an installed
slicer, with remembered mesh format and target. Use the detected target or the native application chooser. This
workflow requires no separate bridge process or pairing token. A launch failure preserves the mesh;
use **Show mesh in folder** for manual recovery. The static browser downloads the same mesh for
manual opening. Discovery, a successful spawn, import, and physical printing are different outcomes.

The legacy authenticated loopback bridge remains an explicit source CLI compatibility workflow,
documented in `docs/3d-printing.md`; it is not required by the product UI. No native slicer-launch MCP
tool is advertised. Use the visible supported handoff within the person's authorization and report
which outcome actually occurred.

When acceptance requires slicing, inspect the actual opened file, scale, orientation, printer/process/filament profile, and requested preview in the chosen slicer. Use an explicitly requested printer/slicer workflow for further operations; this skill itself grants no printer, upload, publication, or paid-service authority.

name: vibeshape-inspection
description: Inspect a VibeShape model or draft for dimensions, authored intent, body roles, topology, and geometry failures using bounded MCP reads and exact preview. Use for CAD result verification and target selection, not source-code debugging.
---

# VibeShape inspection

Use [vibeshape-use](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-use/SKILL.md) for connection or session recovery. Keep inspection read-only unless the user also requested a correction. Preview evaluates disposable draft geometry but does not save it.

## Choose the smallest useful view

| Question | View |
| --- | --- |
| Which project/revision, aggregate exact bounds/volume and model health? | `model_info`; inspect `diagnostics` and retain `measurementDiagnostic` when measurements are unavailable |
| What authored feature/sketch IDs and dependencies exist? | `model_tree`, then complete `model_entity` records for relevant IDs |
| What solved coordinates, DOF, conflicts and usable sketch profiles exist? | `model_sketch_solution` or `draft_sketch_solution` |
| What drives a dimension or fails expression evaluation? | `model_variables` or `draft_variables` |
| Which authored parts/folders or canonical History order? | `model_parts`, `model_folders`, `model_history` |
| Which exact body is available, with which output role? | `model_body_measurements` or `draft_body_measurements` |
| Which exact body faces/edges can be measured or selected by supported features? | `model_body_topology` or `draft_body_topology` |
| What are exact edge lengths, face areas, circular diameters or selected-point distances/angles? | `measure_model` using one or two current body-bound topology references |
| Which edge references can a treatment select? | `model_edges` or `draft_edges` |
| What unsaved intent is in the draft? | `draft_tree`, `draft_entity` at the current draft revision |
| Which assembly instances/mates, frozen frames, local DOF or exact interference? | `model_assembly`, `inspect_assembly`; explicit pairs and occurrence/source topology page |
| Which immutable local component version is available? | `library_items`, `library_version` |
| Does the entire draft rebuild correctly? | `preview_draft`, followed by relevant draft reads |
| Does the visible CAD shape match the requested form and spatial relationships? | `render_preview` at the exact model or owned draft revision |

Use the exact committed revision from `model_info` for model reads; draft reads use the draft's current revision and host-returned draft ID. Follow `nextCursor` until null for a complete requested collection, or stop when a targeted question is answered. Start with `cursor: null` where required. Reduce page size when a response exceeds budget. Do not mix pages across revisions.

Tree dependency summaries include authored sketch inputs for Hole, Loft and Sweep, profile inputs and Revolve axis inputs as well as producer dependencies. Read complete entity records before changing those inputs; a summary does not include all parameters or establish current geometry availability.

## Measure selected topology

Use `measure_model` with `source: "model"` and the current saved `revision`, or `source: "draft"`, owned `draftId` and current draft `revision`. Supply one or two `targets`, each with a stable body-bound edge/face `reference` from the corresponding `model_body_topology` or `draft_body_topology` query. Optional `pointKind` selects `centroid` (default), `start`, `middle`, `end`, or `center`; only analytical points actually available on that element are valid.

The host resolves both selections uniquely against the same exact rebuild. It reports edge `lengthMm` or face `areaMm2`, available circular `radiusMm`/`diameterMm`, analytical direction and selected `pointMm`. Two selections additionally report `pointDistanceMm`, `directionAngleRad` and `parallelPlaneSeparationMm`. Null means the metric is unavailable, not zero. Directions are LINE directions or PLANE normals; the angle is the acute unoriented angle between those vectors, not a general line-to-surface angle. Plane separation measures infinite parallel supporting planes. Selected-point distance is not minimum bounded-face or body clearance. Use assembly interference inspection for its separately supported interference workflow.

Measurement is read-only and does not move the camera, change selection, save the document, modify a draft or renew its expiry. Missing/ambiguous references, an unsupported selected point or stale geometry fail explicitly. Keep the returned revision and units with the reported result; do not replace an unavailable exact result with a pixel estimate.

## Visual inspection

Use `render_preview` after meaningful construction steps and before accepting a shape-dependent
result. Both local and remote MCP return a native PNG image content block plus structured metadata;
the host must pass image content to a vision-capable model. A text-only client cannot inspect the
picture by reading its metadata or base64.

For saved geometry, supply `source: "model"` and `revision` from `model_info`. For unsaved geometry,
supply `source: "draft"`, the owned `draftId`, and its current `revision`. Start with
`quality: "overview"` (also used when omitted): one isometric view within 768 × 576 total pixels.
For small features or shape verification, choose `quality: "detail"`, an exact body target and
relevant views or a close-up. Detail defaults to the legacy labeled isometric/front/right/top
collage within 1024 × 768 total pixels. Either policy may return a smaller raster to fit the
unchanged byte budget; the required top-level `quality` metadata identifies the selected policy,
not an exact resolution guarantee. Explicit one to four unique standard `views` retain their order
independently of quality. Optional `target: { featureId, outputRole }` selects one exact body from
body measurements, including a historical producer output. A missing body fails instead of falling
back to another body.

For an arbitrary angle or a close-up, supply `camera` instead of `views`. `camera.position` and
`camera.target` are world-space XYZ triples in millimeters; `camera.up` is an optional nonzero,
nonparallel orientation vector. Omit it for the default Z-up orientation with a pole-safe fallback.
The projection is orthographic: set `camera.viewHeightMm` to the visible vertical span in millimeters
to zoom into the target region; changing camera distance alone does not zoom. Without that span,
the custom view automatically fits all requested bodies. A close-up intentionally crops the rest
of the model, so retain an overview when evaluating the whole shape. Custom output is labeled
`custom`, and metadata echoes the requested camera. Coordinates and view span are bounded by the
live tool schema. Target and camera remain independent of quality; overview never discards other
bodies unless an exact target is supplied. Never estimate exact dimensions from apparent pixel sizes.

Automation previously defaulted to four views; choose `quality: "detail"` to restore that policy.
Old strict clients can reject the added result field, and old strict servers can reject the request
option. Do not assume mixed-version compatibility.

The renderer fits full CAD body meshes on a separate canvas without changing the user's camera,
selection, saved model or Undo history. It reports document/revision/generation, rendered body count
and `geometryStatus`. An invalid rebuild may show surviving bodies: use numerical diagnostics to
find missing/failed features, then repair the cause. Views cover CAD body geometry rather than
assembly occurrence placement or surface-relief layers; unsupported representations fail explicitly.
Hidden terminal bodies may be included because part visibility is display intent.

Check silhouettes, opening orientation and body placement against the request. Render another
relevant angle when occlusion hides the evidence. Pictures do not establish dimensions, minimum wall
thickness, clearance, exact topology, printability or physical fit; exact measurements remain
authoritative. Retain the corresponding numerical checks. Re-render after edits rather than
combining evidence from different revisions.

## Interpret numerical evidence

Stable feature/part IDs and semantic body output roles identify authored intent. Transient OCCT face/edge indices, kernel handles, display names, and mesh order do not. Use only resolved durable references from the edge-selection tools for modeling. Body-topology tools supply current exact references and content hashes, including unsaved draft producers. Shell openings, planar Extrude endpoints (v6/v7), finite curved-face Extrude endpoints (v7), and Loft v3 end constraints consume their supported face contracts; follow the [modeling reference](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-modeling/references/modeling.md) for each version. These face references are not Hole/Fillet/Chamfer inputs; those operations retain their separate body/edge selection contracts.

Draft body measurements and topology evaluate disposable exact geometry at the owned draft's current revision. Retain returned content hashes and cursor provenance; after a source edit, restart stale discovery. Existing Shell v2 openings can retain unique durable face identity within the same exact body; explicitly reselect missing, ambiguous or unsupported openings. These reads do not save the draft or renew its expiry. `draft_tree`/`draft_entity` are authored records; `draft_edges` selects supported feature edges. Solved sketch profiles are discovered through `model_sketch_solution` or `draft_sketch_solution`. A missing or ambiguous reference must be repaired through a supported selection route, not reconstructed from an index.

Solved sketch reads return status, remaining degrees of freedom and solver provenance on every page. Choose `section: "points"`, `"circles"`, `"failed-constraints"`, `"profiles"` (default), or `"diagnostics"`. Profile pages supply stable boundary selectors, area/perimeter/bounds; use these selectors directly in supported feature tools. Authored point coordinates may differ from solved coordinates; inspection does not save them. Cursors bind an opaque inspection ID and section. Restart with a null cursor after an edit, target change, eviction or cancellation; do not reuse a cursor for another section. An open, ambiguous or conflicting sketch can have no usable profile. Inspect its status and diagnostics instead of inventing a profile index.

Part visibility is display intent; a consumed body may have no current geometry. Aggregate bounds can match while the wrong body or hole is present. For a requested dimensional check, inspect the relevant feature parameters and exact body measurements; use a visual view for spatial relationships that those values cannot establish.

For an invalid preview, locate the first relevant failure in diagnostics, inspect its authored dependencies/constraints/selections, and report the cause supported by that evidence. Null measurements or an inspection error are not zero volume. If correction is authorized, use [vibeshape-modeling](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-modeling/SKILL.md) and preview again after the targeted fix.

`model_info.diagnostics` and `preview_draft.geometry.diagnostics` report feature failures, blocked dependencies, sketch/datum support resolution and external-reference health. Inspect entity IDs, codes, `blockedBy`, `supportFeatureId` and suggested `action`; successful solid measurements can coexist with invalid support diagnostics. `status: unknown` or unavailable diagnostics are not a clean result. A missing or ambiguous support requires inspecting the producer and explicitly reselecting the intended support, not adding unrelated geometry.

## Finish

Report measured values with their declared units, revision, and relevant tolerance. Separate exact kernel validity, visible appearance, slicer interpretation, and physical fit/strength. None implies the others. A request only to inspect does not authorize a commit or an export.

Use `model_measurements` and `draft_measurements` for paged feature measurements. Their `scope` defaults to `terminal`; set `scope: "all"` to inspect failed or blocked upstream features. Begin draft paging with a null cursor; another inspection target or draft edit invalidates the detached catalog.

Assembly inspection omits meshes and frozen source bytes. Topology pages bind an occurrence/source to its body and pin revision; use only uniquely resolved analytical recipes for frame binding. Relinking requires fresh selection. Local DOF is mobility at the solved branch, not global uniqueness. Assembly previews retain the original committed base and private draft version; follow the [assembly/library workflow](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-modeling/references/assembly-and-library.md).

name: vibeshape-modeling
description: Create or edit parametric models in VibeShape using named MCP sketch, feature, variable, assembly, and local-library tools. Use for CAD authoring in the application, rather than changing VibeShape source code or generating geometry in another CAD engine.
---

# VibeShape modeling

Establish the session with [vibeshape-use](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-use/SKILL.md) and follow [draft transactions](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-use/references/transactions.md). Read [modeling contracts and recipes](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-modeling/references/modeling.md) for the requested feature family. For assemblies and reusable components, read [assembly and library transactions](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-modeling/references/assembly-and-library.md). Live schemas determine the exact input shape.
For editable printable relief, read [surface texture proposals](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-modeling/references/surface-textures.md). Their native preview and approval path are separate from a CAD draft.
For minimum-mass removal, SIMP topology optimization, or FEM-graded lattices under explicit loads, stress and displacement limits, read
[structural lightweighting](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-modeling/references/lightweighting.md). Both local and paired remote MCP use
the browser numerical worker; a result is a separate mesh snapshot using the connection's approval policy.
For material removal without prescribed loads, read [quick load-free lightweighting](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-modeling/references/quick-lightweighting.md).
Its Gyroid, Schwarz P and Schwarz D geometry reports measured removal and makes no structural performance claim.

Keep successive user requests additive unless the user explicitly cancels or replaces earlier work.
Retain unresolved requirements in the session context, reconcile new steering with active work, and
check all requested outcomes before declaring completion. Report specific blocked items instead of
silently dropping them when a later message arrives.

## Choose design guidance by purpose

| Purpose | Guidance to load |
| --- | --- |
| Every CAD model | The common intent rules below and [modeling contracts and recipes](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-modeling/references/modeling.md) |
| Functional parts, load-bearing details, fits, or mechanisms | [Mechanical design](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-modeling/references/mechanical-design.md) |
| Models intended for 3D printing | [3D-printing design](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-modeling/references/3d-printing.md), using the section for the intended process |
| FDM/FFF insert lids, corner binding, or compliant perimeter retention | [Lid fits and compliant retention](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-modeling/references/lid-fits.md) |
| Assemblies or reusable components | [Assembly and library transactions](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-modeling/references/assembly-and-library.md) |

Combine applicable categories: a printed latch needs both mechanical and printing guidance. Apply manufacturing rules only when the intended process is established; preserve requested appearance and exact source geometry for visualization or reconstruction. For another manufacturing process, use its current process-specific guidance instead of importing FDM rules.

## Author or revise intent

Translate the request into dimensions, units, mating interfaces, target body, and acceptance measurements. Ask only for missing information that changes the design. For reversible choices, state a reasonable assumption and continue. Preserve protected interfaces and existing model intent.

In embedded chat, use the advertised `ask_user_question` interaction tool for a required design
choice and wait for its validated answer before dependent work. Dismissal, cancellation or timeout
provides no answer. This tool is available through the native project's private MCP attachment and
browser API chat; external CAD MCP clients use their host's own question mechanism. Do not assume
that prose phrased as a question creates an interactive form.

Make all editable design dimensions and numeric controls variable-driven by default: lengths, thicknesses, diameters/radii, clearances, offsets, angles, and supported counts. Create or reuse named document variables before their consumers, and retain `#name` references or derived expressions in sketch constraints and feature quantities instead of baking in evaluated numbers. Follow the Variables section of [modeling contracts and recipes](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-modeling/references/modeling.md), including expression support limits and editability checks.

For modifying Revolve or Subtract on a Pattern/Split constituent, use the exact-body contracts in
[modeling contracts and recipes](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-modeling/references/modeling.md); preserve output roles and sibling Parts.

Before constructing a new model or reconstructing a mesh, choose a feature plan using the construction strategy in [modeling contracts and recipes](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-modeling/references/modeling.md). Identify the main profile, actual symmetries, wall-thickness intent and local details. Before writing sketch entities, explicitly decide whether the profile has a supported symmetry axis and how that symmetry will remain associative. Prefer dimensioning one half and constraining its reflected half; explain any need for independently dimensioned halves. Follow the sketch symmetry recipe in the construction strategy, including Bezier control points. Discover required tools before writing; reconsider the plan after a server update exposes previously unavailable operations.

Read the relevant complete features, sketches, and variables before editing. Prefer changing an existing parameter or variable over reconstructing the model. Use named create/update tools inside a single draft for a coherent edit, followed by exact preview and the ordinary review/commit path. Do not make a new part beside an old one when the request is to revise the old part.

Plan the final independent parts before creating construction solids. A container and its removable lid
normally remain two independent terminal solids; do not fuse them together to reduce a browser count.
Fuse attached details into their intended part and subtract cutters with the appropriate tool-retention
setting. Prefer one associative pattern over manually copying the same detail. Inspect `model_parts`
and exact body measurements after committing a stage: consumed construction parts and History entries
are not additional printable components. Report the terminal part/body count separately from the
number of authored operations.

For a correction, update the existing primitive, sketch, feature, or variable through its available
named `update_*` or variable tool, retaining its ID and dependencies. Do not append another feature
merely to compensate for an editable parameter. When history cleanup is explicitly requested, inspect
dependencies and consumers first; use supported `remove_feature`, `remove_sketch`, or suppression only
for verified redundant intent and validate the complete result before committing. Do not silently
delete user-authored intent or flatten editable geometry. Use the organization workflow
for reviewed `move_history_item` with dependency and folder invariants; automatic feature consolidation
is not exposed. History
folders organize a contiguous range without changing feature order or geometry.

Use the [inspection skill](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-inspection/SKILL.md) to choose targets and diagnose exact preview. Fix the failing feature or constraint; do not delete unrelated geometry or relax constraints simply to obtain a green result. Existing selected edge treatments and body-scoped holes must retain their selection scope.

## Capability boundaries

For an authorized STEP/STP/BREP/STL/3MF source import, read [native source import](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-modeling/references/native-import.md).
For SVG/DXF editable sketch import, read [planar source import](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-modeling/references/planar-import.md).
Its upload, inspection and approval flow is separate from CAD draft construction; it does not accept
caller source hashes or bypass ordinary atomic persistence.

For sketch-backed features, discover solved profile selectors with `model_sketch_solution` or `draft_sketch_solution` at the exact current revision. Inspect native status and failed constraint IDs when profiles are absent; never derive a persistent profile index from display order.

Current local and paired remote MCP cover Box, Cylinder, Cone, Sphere, Torus and Pyramid create/update; sketch, Extrude, Revolve, Hole, Fillet, Chamfer, Datum Plane, Boolean subtraction, Union, Compound, Mirror, linear/circular body Pattern, Shell, Split, Sweep, Loft, custom Thread, and the twelve-kind FDM family create/update; variables; assembly definitions/instances/mates; immutable local-library authoring; inspection; drafts; feature/sketch removal; explicit feature suppression; project rename; and authored metadata. Arbitrary reference planes/axes use the additive `create_reference_*`/`update_reference_*` Mirror, Split and body Pattern tools; legacy names keep their original contracts. Named Placement create/update, face-aligned numeric Placement, sketch corner fillet/chamfer, and editable sketch text create/update/detach are also available. Check discovery before using any operation.

For printed-part reinforcement, reliefs, fastener fits, enclosure joints, membranes, and calibration coupons, follow the FDM section of [modeling contracts and recipes](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-modeling/references/modeling.md).

For committed Undo/Redo, follow the [saved-change History workflow](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-organization/SKILL.md). Registered primitive tools and lifecycle tools use the contracts in the modeling reference; Wedge is not a registered primitive. Feature create/update tools carry explicit suppression intent; supported CAD suppression and removal use an existing explicit auto-apply grant. Existing records may still be inspected and must survive supported upstream edits. Use the ordinary visible editor for a required unsupported operation when available and authorized; otherwise identify the exact limitation. A sketch-backed Extrude/Revolve is a valid alternative only when it preserves the requested design and editability.

In the visible editor, select a current exact Part or its body/face to reveal the main toolbar Part icons. Place / align faces can calculate a numeric Placement from two uniquely resolved planar faces on different current bodies, with opposing/same normals and a signed offset. Use Pick faces in viewport to pause the numeric preview before selecting the committed moving face. The shared calculation is also available as `create_face_aligned_placement` in an owned CAD draft, using current stable body-face references from `draft_body_topology`. It creates a numeric Placement; later target edits do not reposition the placed source. Do not advertise surface or curved-face mating.

## Accept the model

Before commit, compare exact bounds, volume, body count, intended feature parameters, and diagnostics with the requested outcome. Use `render_preview` for the owned draft after meaningful construction steps and before acceptance when shape or spatial relationships matter; follow [visual inspection](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-inspection/SKILL.md). Repair discrepancies and repeat the affected numerical and visual checks at the new revision. After commit, identify the saved revision and relevant changed parameters. Export or back up only when requested, using [vibeshape-export](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-export/SKILL.md).

# Design for 3D printing

Apply this reference only to models intended for printing. Establish the process, candidate print orientation, material, and critical interfaces before changing manufacturing details. Ask for missing process information only when it changes the design; label reversible assumptions. Read [mechanical design](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-modeling/references/mechanical-design.md) for functional or loaded parts. Live tools and exact preview remain authoritative for CAD operations.

## FDM / FFF

### External corners and motion

Prefer rounded external corners in the layer-plane outline, usually by rounding edges parallel to print Z, when dimensions, fits, contact faces, and appearance permit. Use a meaningful variable-backed radius rather than indiscriminately treating every edge. [Klipper's planner documentation](https://www.klipper3d.org/Kinematics.html#look-ahead) explains corner-speed limits; expecting smoother motion from a rounded outline is an engineering inference, not a measured speedup or evidence about a particular printer's firmware. Small radii remain acceleration-limited. Compare sliced paths/time under unchanged settings only when a performance claim matters.

Distinguish these vertical corners from bed-facing edge rounds: a bottom fillet can create a steep early overhang. Prefer a suitable chamfer there when function permits, preserving adequate bed contact. [Prusa's modeling guidance](https://help.prusa3d.com/article/modeling-with-3d-printing-in-mind_164135) describes this orientation-dependent tradeoff.

### Orientation and supported growth

Choose orientation before detailing. Balance layer-direction loading, surface finish, bed contact, and support removal. Inspect roofs, horizontal holes, short bridges, and disconnected starting regions in that frame. Consider sloped or teardrop roofs only if their shape preserves the required interface. Splitting a part may reduce supports but adds a joint to assess. Overhang angles and bridge spans are profile-dependent trial limits, not universal pass criteria. See [Prusa's orientation and support guidance](https://help.prusa3d.com/article/modeling-with-3d-printing-in-mind_164135).

### Walls and small details

Relate walls, ribs, text, and small radii to the intended extrusion widths and layer height. Inspect sliced continuity of critical features. Do not require every wall to be an exact nozzle-width multiple: [Arachne](https://help.prusa3d.com/article/arachne-perimeter-generator_352769) adapts extrusion width, but can still omit or widen small features. Printable minimums do not establish structural sufficiency.

### Fits and assembly

Separate nominal CAD dimensions from calibrated hole/fit allowances. Use representative coupons for critical clearances; consider post-machining when required accuracy cannot be established by printing. Preserve access to holes and fasteners. Small loaded pins may benefit from a root radius or a separate hardware pin. Account for first-layer expansion at bed-level mating edges without stacking unverified CAD and slicer compensation. [Protolabs Network's FDM guide](https://www.hubs.com/knowledge-base/how-design-parts-fdm-3d-printing/) discusses these issues; its numeric examples are not universal limits.

For insert-style lids and covers, read [lid fits and compliant retention](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-modeling/references/lid-fits.md)
for corner relief, flexible corner segments, and perimeter grip fins. Distinguish
rigid clearance from intentional spring contact and validate the expected fit range.

## Resin and other processes

For SLA/MSLA, use the intended machine/resin guide for feature limits and support orientation. Hollowing must account for drainage, cleaning access, and cups in the build orientation; FDM corner-motion advice does not transfer to a resin exposure process. [Formlabs' SLA orientation guidance](https://formlabs.com/support/Model-Orientation/) discusses orientation and drain holes. Its [Form 2 design limits](https://formlabs.com/global/support/Design-Specs/) are tied to that machine, resin, and layer thickness, not all resin printers.

For SLS/MJF or another process, retrieve the actual provider/material design rules before adopting thickness, clearance, or cavity constraints. Do not silently substitute another process to avoid a design limitation.

## Evidence and delivery

Inspect exact final geometry and residual sections, then use [the export workflow](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-export/SKILL.md) for requested files. Check mesh units and curve resolution on the exported artifact, not only the shaded viewport. Record support needs or missing slicer evidence honestly. A valid solid, a clear preview, and a successful slice are distinct from physical fit and print success. Do not launch a print or change printer settings from modeling authorization alone.

Primary sources above were checked on 2026-10-08. Recheck machine-specific claims when choosing actual production limits; the motion recommendation is a qualified synthesis of planner behavior and the requested design preference.

# Assembly and local component library

Use the [model-write approval policy](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-use/references/session.md)
for the current connection. Manual review instructions below apply to external MCP clients;
library publication remains separately reviewed for every connection.

Discover the named tools and their live schemas in the paired local or remote MCP session. Read
`model_info`, then `model_assembly` at its committed revision. Assembly writes have a separate owned
draft; ordinary CAD `create_draft` and its command IDs do not apply to this workflow.

## Author an assembly

1. Call `create_assembly_draft` with the current `baseRevision`. Retain the returned `draftId`, original
   `baseRevision` and private `draftVersion`. Every successful named mutation returns the next version;
   preview retains it. Always use the latest returned tuple. Drafts expire after five minutes of
   inactivity and belong to one paired actor. A document edit requires a fresh draft.
2. Use named definition, instance and joint create/update/remove tools. Obtain source part IDs and body
   roles from `model_parts`, and exact content hashes from `model_body_measurements`. Definitions capture
   frozen source authority inside the controller. Caller-supplied pins, closures, bytes, document
   snapshots, approval flags and file paths are unsupported.
3. Existing assembly v1 retains its strict grounded-forest rules. Explicit `upgrade_assembly` converts
   it to v2 with numeric frame seeds; use v2 for closed loops, multiple mates per occurrence, passive
   drives, cylindrical or ball joints. Every connected component needs a grounded occurrence.
   Instance/joint IDs use UUIDv7. Rigid poses use millimeters and normalized XYZW quaternions; angles
   use radians. Frames preserve orientation and cannot introduce reflection.
4. Run `preview_assembly_draft`. A successful preview is unsaved. Inspect occurrence bounds, local
   degrees of freedom, residual and redundant joint IDs. Passive mobility is valid; it does not prove
   global uniqueness. Conflicting mates, nonconvergence, unsupported budgets and invalid topology fail
   closed. Repair the relevant named records and preview again. Never remove unrelated constraints
   merely to obtain success.
5. Call `commit_assembly_draft` and apply the ordinary browser review. External assembly clients
   require manual Apply, including a session with CAD auto-apply enabled. Library writes require
   manual review for every connection. The exact solver runs
   again after approval before the revision CAS. Edits staged after a review starts cannot share its
   approval. A successful receipt identifies the saved revision and one Undo checkpoint.

Use `discard_assembly_draft` for unwanted proposals. Definition/instance removals expose explicit
`cascade` intent; inspect dependent instances and mates before requesting it.

## Motion studies and visible playback

The Assembly browser lists joints by endpoint and exposes Drive for revolute, prismatic and cylindrical
coordinates. The visible motion panel runs a bounded disposable sweep through the real solver; Apply
saves one solved coordinate and locks that coordinate as a drive. Seek, reverse, sample count, relative
speed and cancellable loop controls do not imply real-time physics or a promised frame rate. A loop
solves its first cycle and replays the cached solved poses, bounded to 256 poses and 64 MiB of meshes.
Reset, project changes and revision changes discard disposable results. Interference uses the saved
assembly and does not prove that an entire motion is collision-free.

The labelled **Motion studies** toolbar control opens new/saved studies and Drive actions.
**Play animation** starts playback inside an open study or Drive panel. An assembly without movable
joints explains why a study cannot start; Model bodies alone are not a kinematic assembly. The UI
labels tracks with named component endpoints and edits values in project display units (degrees by
default); MCP payloads retain radians and millimeters. Per-track graphical keys support bounded time
dragging and keyboard edits; exact key values remain available in **Edit keys**. Confirm numeric edits with Enter or blur before Save/playback. UI duration changes
rescale all key times, rejecting changes that would merge distinct times. **Copy to another joint** copies keys to an unused same-kind coordinate with a
constant angular/translation value offset, checked against target limits. Copies are independent;
this does not add a gear coupling or a general temporal phase relation. Playback and exports remain
visible-UI workflows with the ordinary preview/Apply distinction.

Use `model_assembly` to read saved `motionStudies`. In an owned assembly draft, stage
`create_assembly_motion_study`, `update_assembly_motion_study` or `remove_assembly_motion_study`, then
preview and request ordinary manual Apply. A study has stable UUIDv7 study/track IDs, a duration up to
3600 seconds and 1–64 tracks. Each track selects a stable joint and `angle` (radians) or `translation`
(millimeters), with 2–256 strictly increasing key times inside the duration. The document permits 32
studies and 16384 keys in total. Track coordinates must be unique. Linear interpolation holds the
first/last values outside their key interval. All tracks evaluate simultaneously; cylindrical angle
and translation merge into one joint replacement. Missing joints, changed joint kinds or out-of-limit
keys require repairing/removing tracks in the same transaction. Saving study intent does not apply
its pose or upgrade a legacy assembly.

Read `sample_assembly_motion_study` at the exact committed revision to solve 2–64 samples, optionally
in reverse. Select 1–32 occurrence IDs to bound the response. An optional trace selects one source
index and local point in millimeters; the returned point uses its actual solved geometry frame. Any
solver, limit, cancellation, revision or response-budget failure returns no partial sample result.
Reduce sample/occurrence counts when the 128 KiB response budget is exceeded. Sampling never saves a
pose. Apply a desired pose through ordinary owned joint updates and browser review if requested.

MCP exposes study authoring and exact sampling, not continuous UI playback or image downloads. The
visible study panel exports actual solved JSON/CSV poses and optional point traces, or up to 64 PNG
frames in a ZIP with one fixed camera and a manifest. GIF encoding, contact response, gears/cams and
new mate types are outside this animation contract.

## Select topology frames

Use `inspect_assembly` at the committed revision with an explicit `topology` occurrence/source page.
It returns bounded frozen-source references without meshes or kernel indices. A binding includes that
page's source index, body, pin revision, uniquely resolved reference and analytical geometry recipe,
plus a finite origin hint and X direction. Supported recipes are planar, cylindrical and spherical
faces, circular/arc edges and vertices. Numeric parent/child frames become offsets from the resolved
geometry frame. Mesh occurrences support numeric frames only.

Missing, ambiguous, unsupported or stale topology requires explicit reselection. Relinking increments
the definition pin revision; old bindings do not silently follow the replacement. For exact interference,
request explicit instance pairs through `inspect_assembly`; overlapping meshes report unsupported.

## Reuse the local library

Read `library_items` and `library_version` at the paired committed revision. Version views contain
immutable content identity and metadata, not frozen document closures or raw bytes. Save a current
part/definition with `save_library_definition`; use `expectedMetadataRevision: null` for a new item,
or the current metadata revision for an existing item. Publication requires manual review.
`update_library_metadata` uses the same metadata CAS and does not rewrite immutable versions.

Inside an owned assembly draft, `insert_library_version` requires an explicit immutable version and
`mode: copy` or `reference`, plus definition/instance IDs, names and a grounded pose. Reference mode
retains a pinned library binding; copy mode does not. `relink_library_definition` selects a new version
for an existing reference. `detach_library_definition` removes its binding while retaining frozen
content. Neither operation follows a moving library head automatically. Preview and commit the assembly
through its ordinary review path. Source closure bytes remain repository/controller-owned throughout.

Report saved revision, local mobility and the selected immutable library version. Export an assembly
through the authorized visible editor when requested; these authoring tools do not expose a named
assembly export operation.

# FDM/FFF lid fits and compliant retention

Use this reference for an FDM/FFF insert-style lid, plug, or removable cover that
must fit inside a measured opening. Establish FDM/FFF as the intended process before
applying these construction and calibration checks. For resin, SLS, MJF, or another
process, use its own design guidance instead. Combine [mechanical design](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-modeling/references/mechanical-design.md)
with the FDM/FFF section of [3D-printing design](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-modeling/references/3d-printing.md).
Threaded, gasketed, and positive-lock closures need their own interface design;
do not replace them with friction fins without preserving the requested function.

## Design principle

Separate the rigid locating geometry from the contact that provides retention.
A rigid lid perimeter can bind at a corner or along an entire wall when the
opening, print, or alignment varies. First give the rigid core sufficient
clearance. Then choose where contact should remain: straight wall regions,
flexible corner tabs, or distributed spring fins. Compliance accommodates a
bounded size variation; its useful travel and retention depend on geometry,
material, print orientation, temperature, and time under load.

| Observed need | Construction | Acceptance condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Corners bind while straight walls already fit | Recess the corner contact regions | Corner clearance throughout insertion, with wall support preserved |
| Local corner contact should yield during insertion | Isolate attached corner tabs with slots | Free tabs can bend into clearance space without hitting a stop or separating from the lid |
| Retention must tolerate variation around the opening | Clear the rigid core and add distributed cantilever fins | Fin contact at the largest opening and recoverable travel at the smallest opening |

Choose the simplest construction that meets the required retention and removal
behavior. Do not add all three treatments automatically. A freely removable
cover may need clearance and a stop without elastic interference.

## Establish the mating interface

Measure the opening at the insertion depth, including its smallest/largest
expected span, corner radii, taper, lip, and insertion stop. Distinguish measured
values from nominal CAD and assumptions. For a physical container, request the
critical measurements when they are unavailable; an unscaled image is not a measurement.
Identify removal access, retention needs, repeated-use expectations, and the
intended material/process before choosing a compliant detail.

Keep the container and lid as separate final parts. Define named variables for
the opening profile, per-side rigid clearance, insertion depth, lid thickness,
corner relief, and any spring or fin geometry before creating their consumers.
For opposed straight walls, a rigid insert span is the opening span minus twice
the per-side clearance. For curved or irregular profiles, construct the intended
normal clearance rather than uniformly scaling the outline. Preserve the user's
accepted surfaces and sealing requirements.

## Choose the contact strategy

### Corner clearance relief

Use local corner cutbacks when the corners bind while the straight walls already
have the intended clearance. Remove contact only from the offending region and
retain adequate wall thickness, lid support, and insertion stops. This reduces
corner interference; it does not create a spring or fix an oversized rigid span.
In plan view, replace the contacting corner of the insertion skirt with a recessed
arc, chamfer, or notch that clears the actual container corner over the engagement
depth. Keep the lid's top overhang or stop intact when it provides support.
Parameterize relief width/depth or radius separately from straight-wall clearance;
a smaller corner radius alone does not guarantee that the contact moved inward.

Use `create_fdm` / `update_fdm` with `kind: corner-relief` only when a positioned
cylindrical cut matches the requested relief. Otherwise author the cutback with
a supported constrained sketch and subtractive feature. Inspect every affected
corner and the remaining sections; do not use an arbitrary whole-body edge fillet
as a substitute for removing the actual contact.

### Integral corner flexure tabs

Use slots or relief cuts that leave an attached corner segment free to bend in
the required contact direction. Preserve its root and a clear deflection space;
a notch that leaves a fully backed wall does not establish useful compliance.
For a skirt attached to a lid plate, slots can start at the skirt's free insertion
edge and stop before the plate, leaving a continuous root. Place the slots so
the corner contact belongs to a defined flexible tab, with room to move toward
the core. Keep a connected load path from that tab to the plate; cutting through
the entire root creates a loose fragment instead of a flexure.
Parameterize free length, bending thickness, slot width/depth, root radius, and
contact projection. Use the tab's free length and bending thickness to tune
compliance independently of the rigid core clearance. Round slot ends and roots
where function and available geometry allow; inspect the residual section after
the cuts.

Build this with supported sketch-driven cuts unless a live feature contract
actually matches the geometry. A cylindrical `corner-relief` alone is not a
general slotted-corner spring. Treat force, recoverable strain, creep, and fatigue
as material/process-dependent quantities requiring separate evidence.

### Distributed cantilever grip fins

Keep the rigid lid core clear of the opening and add attached perimeter fins as
the intended contact regions. Provide a lead-in and space for the fins to deflect
along the insertion path. Parameterize fin projection, thickness, free length,
spacing, and engagement depth; maintain a root connected to the core. Distribute
fins over useful wall regions, avoiding interference between corner details.
Each fin needs an attached root, a free contact portion, and an unobstructed
bending path. Choose its cross-section and direction so insertion bends that
free portion rather than compressing a short, fully supported rib. Chamfer or
round the leading contact edge where appropriate, and keep the insertion stop
separate from the spring travel.

For a centered symmetric fit, the fin-tip envelope must reach the largest opening
that needs contact, while required travel at the smallest opening must remain
within demonstrated recoverable deflection. Check each wall/profile direction;
a final assembled view alone does not establish an unobstructed insertion path.

For two opposed, identical fins, use the following centered fit model along each
relevant span. It is a geometric travel budget, not a force or strength model:

- `opening_min`, `opening_max`: smallest and largest expected opening spans.
- `core_span`: rigid core span; `(opening_min - core_span) / 2` must retain the
  required rigid clearance at the tightest opening.
- `fin_envelope`: unloaded span across opposing fin tips.
- `deflection_min = (fin_envelope - opening_max) / 2`: minimum per-fin deflection;
  positive contact preload requires a value above zero.
- `deflection_max = (fin_envelope - opening_min) / 2`: maximum per-fin deflection;
  it must fit both the free geometric travel and the established recoverable travel.

Derive these quantities from named variables when supported. Include print
variation in the spans being assessed. If the lid can shift off center, or opposing
fins differ in stiffness, assess unequal travel instead of assuming an equal split.
Do not choose a universal interference allowance or claim sufficient retention
from a positive deflection value alone.

Author one editable fin and use a supported associative pattern or mirror when
the layout warrants it, then fuse attached additions into the lid's single solid.
Inspect terminal bodies so patterned fins do not remain separate printable parts.
The FDM `crush-ribs` tool adds inward ribs to an existing bore; it is not a generic
outward lid-fin tool, and sacrificial crush retention is not equivalent to a
reusable spring. Discover the actual sketch, pattern, and union schemas through
[modeling contracts](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-modeling/references/modeling.md) rather than inventing a dedicated lid tool.

## Accept and calibrate

Use exact preview and [inspection](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-inspection/SKILL.md) to check
rigid clearance, corner cutbacks, attachment roots, deflection spaces, insertion
depth/stops, and the intended terminal part count. Keep checks at the tightest
and loosest expected interface dimensions explicit. Review print orientation,
layer-direction loading, first-layer expansion, and whether slots/fins survive
the intended extrusion width and layer height.

For an uncalibrated fit, propose a small representative perimeter segment or
corner coupon with the same material, orientation, and local geometry. The built-in
FDM calibration coupon is a hole-size ladder, not a lid-fin test. Use ordinary
parametric geometry for a representative specimen. Physical checks should cover
insertion/removal, retention, permanent set, and repeated use as required; record
their actual results before claiming a verified fit. Update the existing fit
variables from that evidence rather than stacking unverified compensation.

Report the chosen strategy, assumptions, changed variables, and remaining physical
checks. CAD validity does not prove sealing, food-contact suitability, or production
reliability. Follow [export delivery](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-export/SKILL.md) when files are
requested; this reference grants no printer operation or print-start authority.

# Structural lightweighting

Use the [model-write approval policy](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-use/references/session.md)
for the current connection. Manual review instructions below apply to external MCP clients.

Use this workflow only when `analyze_lightweighting` and `request_lightweighting` are advertised
and the user authorized preliminary structural analysis or material removal on the paired project.
Both tools run the same browser-owned worker as the editor. They are available on the local and
paired remote transports. They accept no mesh arrays, file paths, scripts, actor or approval flags.

## Capture the source and physical inputs

1. Read `model_info`, then `model_parts` at the same committed revision. Select one current,
   available exact solid Part, retaining its `partId` and body `featureId`/`outputRole`.
2. Read `model_body_measurements` for that body at the same revision and retain its exact
   `contentHash`. Supply all four fields under `source`, with `baseRevision`. Do not guess IDs,
   reuse an earlier body's hash, or select an imported triangle mesh. Surface relief is excluded.
3. Obtain the intended material's Young's modulus and yield strength in MPa, Poisson ratio, and
   density in kg/m³. When advertised, `list_lightweighting_materials` with empty arguments returns
   the same eight named examples as the editor: PLA, PETG, ABS, ASA, PC Blend, Nylon, aluminum
   6061-T6 and stainless steel 304. Inspect source revisions, URLs, specimen/product conditions,
   and limitations; copy the selected entry's `material` into `settings.material` and adjust for
   the actual material/process. A preset name or ID alone does not replace the numeric settings.
   Printed examples are horizontal/XY 100%-infill samples, not Z-direction strength or print
   certification. All listed Poisson ratios are explicitly assumed. Do not invent physical
   properties, treat sample means as certified design allowables, or use TPU as a supported preset.
4. Define axis-aligned support, load and preservation boxes with world-mm `min`/`max` triples,
   or current source surface regions `{kind: "surface", triangleIndices, depthMm}`. Surface
   indices refer only to the exact captured source tessellation at this body/hash/revision and
   `depthMm` defines the inward preservation depth. They are not persistent face identities,
   `TopoRef` IDs or triangle IDs from an imported result. Do not guess indices from render images
   or face order; use explicit current source indices when available, otherwise use physical boxes.
   Supports clamp selected exterior FEM nodes in all directions. Each uniquely named load case
   supplies a nonzero total `forceN` vector in newtons, distributed over complete exterior facets
   inside its region. Loaded facets must not touch support nodes. Verify the regions against the
   current bounds and mesh resolution; they do not follow later source edits.
5. Supply `safetyFactor` (at least 1), `maxDisplacementMm`, `cellSizeMm`, `preserveRegions` (possibly
   empty), and `maxIterations` (0–40). Poisson ratio is limited to 0–0.45. Schema bounds remain
   authoritative. Analysis is limited to 20,000 source triangles, 10,000 source vertices,
   3,000 FEM cells, 5,000 nodes and 8 load cases.

   Optional `obstacleRegions` accepts up to sixteen positive-size world-mm `{min,max}` boxes.
   Any closed FEM-cell box intersecting a keep-out box is excluded before baseline analysis,
   including boundary contact and the permitted STL coordinate-rounding margin. Intersections with
   support, load, or preserved cells fail explicitly.
   Exclusion can disconnect or invalidate the baseline. Mass targets refer to the remaining feasible
   baseline; source-volume loss includes excluded material as well as voxelization loss.

   Optional `fdm` supplies `buildDirection` (`+x`, `-x`, `+y`, `-y`, `+z`, or `-z`),
   `supportMode` (`forbidden` or `allowed`), `minFeatureSizeMm`, `layerHeightMm`, and
   `maxOverhangAngleDeg` (0–89 degrees from vertical). Both policies enforce a conservative
   filled-cube bound in solver and captured float32 geometry. Layer height must not exceed voxel
   cell size and the smallest actual raw/float32 build-axis slice for the one-slice support check.
   Exact cell-size equality can fail after rounding; decrease layer height. Both policies enforce the requested
   minimum-feature bound. `forbidden` additionally requires no unsupported area;
   `allowed` reports that area without generating supports. An incompatible baseline fails instead
   of relaxing these limits. No extrusion, bridging, adhesion, infill, or layer-strength simulation
   is implied. Build direction changes the analysis, not the exported mesh coordinates; reproduce
   it during print preparation. Omission keeps the prior structural behavior.

6. `objective` is optional. Omission or `{kind: "minimize-mass"}` retains the existing
   mass-reduction search. `{kind: "maximize-stiffness", retainedMassFraction}` uses a retained
   mass fraction of 0.1–1 relative to the conservative FEM baseline, not the original exact solid.
   It guides removal by increasing maximum cell strain energy across load cases until the rounded mass
   target or another stop condition. This is an approximate stiffness-guided removal heuristic;
   it does not solve a globally optimal minimum-compliance or generative-design problem.

## Select an optimization algorithm

Both paired transports accept optional `settings.algorithm`. Omission keeps feasible cell removal.

- SIMP: `{kind: "simp", volumeFraction, filterRadiusMm, penalty}`. Fraction is 0.1–1 of the
  conservative baseline; filter radius is at least one cell and penalty is 1–5. When also supplying
  a maximize-stiffness objective, its retained fraction must match exactly. Inspect
  `summary.algorithm` for the echoed settings, density iteration/convergence, binary target count,
  achieved count, target status, and projection evaluations. Density convergence does not establish
  that the exported full-solid geometry reached the volume target or a global optimum.
- Adaptive TPMS: `{kind: "adaptive-lattice", lattice, cellPeriodMm, minWallThicknessMm,
  maxWallThicknessMm, skinThicknessMm, field, gamma}`. Types are `gyroid`, `schwarz-p`, and
  `schwarz-d`; field is `strain-energy` or `von-mises`, combined conservatively across cases.
  Period requires at least eight analysis cells and minimum wall at least two; maximum wall lies
  between minimum wall and half the period. Skin is 0 or at least one analysis cell. Gamma is
  0.1–8. Load/support/preserved cells remain protected. Inspect field range, requested wall range,
  conservative occupied-cube feature bound, and projection evidence. Do not call requested wall
  thickness a measured smooth-surface minimum.

Browser and MCP validation require `densityIterations` or `thresholdPasses` to equal
`summary.iterations`, which must not exceed the requested `maxIterations`.
Projection evaluations must fit that search budget (SIMP permits one additional restoration
projection) and match total FEM evaluations after baseline, density solves, and final validation.
A zero search budget permits no projection.

Every accepted result is reanalyzed as full-solid cells for every load case. Relaxed SIMP metrics
or the source field cannot substitute for final feasibility. Underresolved walls and incompatible
protected geometry fail explicitly; never weaken user constraints to obtain success. Ordinary
resource limits, stale-source protection, cancellation, review, Apply, and Undo remain authoritative.
The multi-candidate study remains editor-only; these tools run one selected algorithm/scenario.

## Analyze and request a snapshot

`analyze_lightweighting` computes bounded baseline and feasible-candidate evidence without editing
the model or requesting Apply. `maxIterations: 0` evaluates the baseline without removal. Examine
the baseline and optimized volume/mass, worst stress, displacement, achieved safety factor and
every named case. The feasible baseline must already satisfy all requested stress/safety and
displacement constraints; an infeasible or underconstrained model fails instead of returning an
accepted candidate. Compliance is reported per case as analysis evidence. The search ranks cells
by the maximum strain energy across cases, rechecks physical feasibility after accepted removal,
and reduces infeasible removal batches; it does not compare full candidate compliance to establish
maximum stiffness.

For requested FDM constraints, inspect `summary.fdm`: its echoed `settings` must match the request,
and `baseline`/`optimized` report `unsupportedAreaMm2`, `requiresSupports`,
`minFeatureSizeBoundMm`, and `buildHeightMm`. The minimum-feature bound must satisfy the request;
support-free evidence must report zero unsupported area. Area is not support volume, support
accessibility, or a physical printability certificate. Manual review shows the complete FDM settings.

For a stiffness-guided objective, inspect `summary.objective`: requested `retainedMassFraction`,
`targetMassKg`, `targetCellCount`, `achievedRetainedMassFraction` and `targetStatus`. The target
cell count rounds upward from the baseline fraction. `reached` means the rounded cell target was
reached and uses `target-mass-reached` termination; `not-reached` reports a remaining target gap
with a warning. Do not describe a partial target as attained. A baseline-only run with a retained
fraction of 1 can already be `reached` without material removal or a new snapshot.

Inspect `sourceVolumeMm3` and `sourceVolumeLossFraction`: conservative interior cells already omit
some original material before optimization. Baseline-to-candidate saving is separate from that
discretization loss. A finer cell size can improve source approximation while exceeding the cell
or node budget. Errors require correcting the physical inputs, regions or resolution; do not weaken
the user's limits merely to obtain a successful result.

When the user authorized creating the result, call `request_lightweighting` with the same complete
inputs and an English `label`. It computes again against the captured committed body. An improved
candidate is encoded as a private immutable STL SourceAsset, inspected and shown in the ordinary
browser mesh preview together with the material, constraints, regions and analysis evidence.
External clients require manual Apply/Reject, including CAD auto-apply sessions. Keep the tool call open
while the user reviews it; no caller approval substitutes for browser Apply.

Apply performs one ordinary atomic import transaction and creates one Undo entry, retaining the
original Part. The saved revision can advance by several command revisions within that transaction.
The response contains bounded `summary` plus the committed `snapshot` identity: `uploadId`,
`featureId`, `outputRoles`, `documentId`, base and saved revisions. Mesh arrays never traverse the
MCP broker. A `no-improvement` response has `snapshot: null` and creates neither review nor model
mutation. Do not retry an uncertain successful Apply blindly.

The worker has a three-minute compute budget; transport budgets are scoped to these tools.
The private import/review lease expires after five minutes. Cancellation, session revocation,
changed revision/body/hash, rejected or expired review prevents mutation. Cancellation after an
atomic persistence transaction has been accepted must report its actual outcome. Re-read the
source identity and physical regions after a stale-source error.

## Acceptance limits

Binary STL capture is gated before evidence publication: coordinate rounding must stay within one
millionth of the analysis cell size and the rounded mesh must remain a valid manufacturing solid.
For `serialization-precision`, move the source closer to the origin or choose coarser cells, then
recapture its current revision/body/hash. Do not apply rounded geometry against earlier metrics.

This is an independent unsmoothed FEM-cell mesh snapshot, not an exact CAD feature or live
regenerating topology optimization. The bounded material-removal search does not establish a
global minimum. Results use preliminary isotropic small-deformation linear elasticity and the
specified loads/constraints; they do not establish physical strength, fatigue, buckling, contact,
manufacturability or print performance. Keep those limits visible when presenting the metrics.
Export or back up the committed snapshot only when requested, through `vibeshape-export`.

The editor also offers a bounded multi-material/mass-target Generative Design study. It is not a
new paired MCP tool: these tools still analyze/request one scenario at a time. Do not claim automatic
study comparison or candidate selection through MCP. The editor study does not add manufacturing
constraints, CAD reconstruction, global-optimum guarantees, or physical strength certification.

Apply keeps the editable source in the Parts tree and hides it in the same atomic transaction
as the new mesh, preventing it from covering the result. One Undo removes the mesh and restores
the source visibility. Show the source again through its normal visibility control when needed.

# Mechanical design

Use this guidance for functional parts, load-bearing details, fits, and mechanisms, whether printed or manufactured another way. Combine it with [3D-printing design](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-modeling/references/3d-printing.md) only when printing is intended.

## Loads and transitions

Identify where loads enter and react, and which sections bend, peel, or twist. Prefer rounded transitions over sharp corners where feasible and consistent with the task, especially at internal corners, section changes, and the roots of load-bearing ribs, brackets, pins, and snap arms, to reduce stress concentrations.

Choose radii that preserve required dimensions, mating surfaces, clearances, and remaining load-bearing sections; retain sharp edges when their function requires them. Use supported profile arcs or scoped Fillet features with named radius variables. Inspect exact preview and critical sections after treatment. Successful geometry alone does not establish strength or fatigue life.

## Fits and movement

Keep accepted contact geometry and the provenance of critical dimensions explicit. Distinguish running clearance, intentional contact, and elastic interference. Inspect the insertion/removal path, retention, and tool access rather than checking only the final assembled pose. Avoid changing a retaining shoulder or datum merely to simplify construction.

For flexible mechanisms, separate a geometric deformation or clearance check from an elasticity or cycle-life claim. Use applicable material/process data, a justified calculation, or physical evidence for structural acceptance; do not infer it from a render.

# Modeling contracts and recipes

Use the [model-write approval policy](vibeshape://agent-skills/vibeshape-use/references/session.md)
for the current connection. Manual review instructions below apply to external MCP clients;
library publication remains separately reviewed for every connection.

## Choose a construction

Recover design intent rather than tracing tessellation. Identify straight, circular and rotational regions, repeated geometry, openings and protected interfaces. Use a small number of dimensioned profiles and features when they reproduce the requested shape. Prefer line/arc profiles over dense sampled boundaries for analytical geometry; use additional Loft sections only where the shape or an agreed error bound requires them.

For an elongated enclosure, consider Extrude for the straight section, Revolve for rotational ends, and Mirror for genuinely symmetric regions. Join the exterior into one solid, then use Shell when the intended interior is a constant-thickness offset with selected openings. Model holes, lips, reinforcements and asymmetric ends separately. A simple planar capsule may need only one outline Extrude and Shell. Neither recipe establishes that an arbitrary source mesh has constant thickness or symmetric ends.

Compare outer and inner sections before choosing Shell for a reconstruction. Use explicit inner profiles and subtraction when variable thickness, mating surfaces or exact source geometry cannot be reproduced by Shell, or when exact Shell preview demonstrates a kernel limitation. Preserve an authored interior instead of replacing it with a convenient uniform wall. State the specific reason for a more complex construction; a missing tool at an earlier connection is not evidence that it remains unavailable after an update.

Check a representative section and one end before duplicating the construction. Keep the plan proportional to the geometry: repeated independently authored profiles, mirrored numeric coordinates and many support planes are signals to reconsider reuse, symmetry or a simpler feature. A Boolean or solver failure requires inspecting the failing operation and diagnostics before adding more geometry. Report a demonstrated tool/kernel limitation rather than silently accepting a different shape.

### Decide sketch symmetry before placing points

Before creating a sketch, state whether the intended profile is symmetric, its axis and which half owns the dimensions. Use symmetry only when the source or requested design supports it; photographs alone do not establish a mating interface's symmetry. If independent halves are necessary, identify the asymmetric detail or demonstrated capability limitation before duplicating their dimensions.

For a symmetric outline, dimension one half and add a stable construction line as the symmetry axis. Keep the reflected geometry associative with `symmetric` constraints linking corresponding point pairs to that line. Include both cubic Bezier control points as well as endpoints, since symmetric endpoints alone do not make a symmetric curve. Reuse points on the axis or constrain them to it, and retain a closed connected profile. Do not also give the reflected points independent X/Y dimensions that duplicate the symmetry equations. The reflected half still contains point and curve entities; its positions are derived rather than independently dimensioned.

The editor's sketch Mirror creates reflected entities with symmetry constraints. Named MCP `create_mirror` and `create_reference_mirror` operate on bodies, not sketch entities. When a named sketch Mirror is absent, inspect the live `create_sketch`/`update_sketch` schema: a complete sketch record accepting `symmetric` can express the same point relationships. Use a body Mirror only when the feature plan calls for a reflected solid. A missing convenience tool is not evidence that associative sketch symmetry is unavailable.

Inspect the solved profile and editability before committing: changing a source-side dimension must update its paired points and Bezier controls while preserving the intended single closed profile. For an existing model, read constraints and dependent features first; replacing duplicate dimensions with symmetry is a separate authorized CAD edit, not an automatic instruction upgrade.


Choose one model coordinate frame before authoring: identify the origin, principal axes, symmetry planes and feature offsets. Prefer centering a new standalone part about an appropriate origin or symmetry axis unless the user requires another frame. For a reconstruction, preserve the source frame only when alignment, mating or another acceptance requirement depends on it; matching an arbitrary mesh bounding-box minimum is not itself a reason to translate every body.

Author sketches, primitive origins and feature axes in their intended locations when the advertised contracts support them. Add Placement only for a real downstream positioning or orientation requirement, and explain that purpose in the feature label. Check a sketch-line axis, supported datum or explicit primitive origin before creating geometry at zero and immediately moving it. Do not add repeated Placement features to make the model sit beside the origin or improve its viewport composition; use camera Fit instead. Do not remove an existing Placement until inspecting its consumers, references and exact before/after bounds proves that the design intent is preserved.

## Manual editor operations

The editor also offers planar **Press Pull** and saved part **Material and Color** through viewport
selection actions. They currently have no named MCP authoring tools; do not invent tool names or
substitute extrusion-distance editing for direct face editing. Existing MCP geometry/history edits
preserve V6 part appearance by authored PartId, and native backups retain it. Appearance presets are
visual metadata, not structural material or density assignments. Inspect the live schemas before
claiming a new transport capability.

## Registered primitives

Box keeps its existing `create_box` millimeter shorthand and adds `update_box` with a complete
typed `parameters` record. Cylinder, pointed Cone, Sphere, ring Torus and regular Pyramid each
have named create/update tools using their registered domain schemas. Supply quantity dimensions,
quantity `{ x, y, z }` origin, applicable `centered`, explicit `suppressed`, the label to retain,
stable feature ID, fresh command ID and current owned draft revision. These independent primitives
accept no dependencies or topology references. Read the full existing feature before updating;
preserve its identity and raw expressions. The live schemas define bounds and required fields.
Torus requires major radius greater than minor radius; Pyramid takes 3–64 integer sides and a
circumradius. Wedge and truncated Cone are not registered primitive contracts.

Inspect exact preview volume, bounds and body count before commit. A valid matching CAD auto-apply
grant covers all shipped first-party primitive families and supported feature versions, including
Extrusion v6/v7, Mirror and Shell. Unsupported versions, extensions and import feature targets
remain outside the grant.

## Feature and sketch lifecycle

`remove_feature` and `remove_sketch` stage ordinary destructive removal by stable ID.
Dependencies block removal with `feature-in-use` or `sketch-in-use`; the rejected command does
not advance the draft revision. Inspect the owning records and explicitly remove or retarget
their consumers first. These tools never cascade or discard model-reference intent. The editor's History Delete can disconnect affected inputs and retain downstream repair recipes, but this is not the removal contract of these MCP tools. Do not infer MCP support from the visible editor action.

`set_feature_suppressed` takes an explicit boolean, preserving the remaining authored record.
Suppression can block downstream geometry; exact preview exposes that failure and must be repaired
